answer:
Yes. A large international review of 11 major cardiovascular outcome trials found that GLP-1 receptor agonists reduced the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events by about 13%, including heart attack, stroke, and cardiovascular death [2]. That review, reported May 21, 2026, followed patients on average for nearly three years, and the drugs studied included semaglutide, liraglutide, and dulaglutide [2].

A real-world study reported November 21, 2025, found that both tirzepatide and semaglutide strongly protect the heart, reducing heart attack, stroke, and death in adults with type 2 diabetes [3]. The same study noted that earlier studies had already shown semaglutide lowers the likelihood of major cardiovascular events such as heart attacks and strokes [3]. It found only small differences between the two drugs in cardiovascular protection among at-risk populations [3].

Network meta-analyses cited in a systematic review suggest semaglutide has the highest probability of cardiovascular benefits among GLP-1 receptor agonists [1]. Another network meta-analysis found semaglutide and albiglutide reduce major adverse cardiac events more than other agents in their classes [1].
